title: Does a heavy ball sink?
hook: Same 500 g ball, made bigger and smaller. What does the water do with it?

knows: that some things sink and some float
doesNotKnow: that density is mass per volume
that floating depends on density compared with the liquid's, not on mass

misconception: Heavy objects sink and light objects float.
objective: The learner can explain that an object floats when its mass per volume is less than the liquid's: a 500 g ball of 800 cm³ is 0.625 g/cm³ and floats in water (about 1.0 g/cm³), while the same 500 g squeezed below 500 cm³ sinks.

claims.text: Water is about 1.0 g/cm³ (0.99997 g/cm³ at 4 °C, 0.998 g/cm³ at 20 °C).
claims.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Properties of water in the range 0-100 °C' (density table).

claims.text: Density is mass divided by volume; a 500 g ball of 800 cm³ is 0.625 g/cm³.
claims.source: Definition of density (IUPAC Gold Book, 'mass density'); 500 g / 800 cm³ = 0.625 g/cm³.

claims.text: A solid object sinks if it is denser than the liquid, floats if it is less dense, and stays put at any depth (hovers) if the densities match.
claims.source: Archimedes' principle: buoyant force = weight of displaced liquid. Any introductory physics text, e.g. Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 14 (Fluids).

claims.text: With mass fixed at 500 g, the crossover is at 500 cm³: smaller sinks, larger floats.
claims.source: 500 g / V = 1.0 g/cm³ gives V = 500 cm³.

claims.text: A floating object has the same fraction of its volume under water as its density divided by water's: 0.625, five eighths (62.5%), for this ball.
claims.source: Floating: weight = buoyancy, so rho_obj x V = rho_water x V_under, V_under / V = 0.625 / 1.0. The stage solves the spherical-cap depth h for (h/r)^2 (3 - h/r)/4 = 0.625 by bisection. | CLAIM FIX 2026-10-13: Stage drawing was wrong (cap sign mirrored: ball drawn 37.5% under at 800 cm3). Fixed Demo.tsx: cy = SURF + (capDepth(rho/RHO_W) - 1) * r, so 62.5% is under water at 800 cm3. Claim text unchanged. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): Archimedes: V_under/V = rho_obj/rho_w = 500/800 = 0.625. Re-checked the 2026-10-13 stage fix: cap fraction h^2(3r-h)/(4r^3) is correct; own bisection gives h/r = 1.168; cy = SURF + (h/r - 1) r puts the ball bottom at SURF + h, so 62.5% is under water. Stage now matches.

claims.text: Heavy ships float for the same reason: their hull encloses so much volume (mostly air) that their average density is below water's.
claims.source: Archimedes' principle applied to a hull; Halliday, Resnick & Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 14.

recall.question: A 200 g block has a volume of 250 cm³. In water (about 1.0 g/cm³) it…
recall.why: Density is 200 / 250 = 0.8 g/cm³, less than water's 1.0, so it floats whatever it weighs.
